asked_fact_assessments.asked_fact: Abstainer must play one main-offer support card or lose one capital.

whole_entry_support.quote: That player must either play 1 card supporting the main offer or lose 1 capital.

grades.rationale: The abstention timing, optional exhaustion cost, and abstainer’s one main-support card or one-capital loss are correct.

grades.label: Correct

asked_fact_assessments.asked_fact: After own main offer, discard Fall Guy to propose own counteroffer.

whole_entry_support.quote: After proposing a main offer, the active player may discard The Fall Guy to propose a counteroffer too.
The Fall Guy is discarded.

asked_fact_assessments.asked_fact: Proceed immediately to Support, bypassing other counteroffer opportunities.

whole_entry_support.quote: Proceed immediately to Support.

asked_fact_assessments.asked_fact: Chief cannot cancel this counteroffer.

whole_entry_support.quote: No. Chief Gorman does not cancel The Fall Guy’s counteroffer.

grades.rationale: The required activation timing is explicitly answered, independently of the phantom scenario metadata: after own main offer. Discard Fall Guy, own counteroffer, immediate Support with no intervening counteroffer opportunity, and Chief immunity are correct.

grades.label: Correct

asked_fact_assessments.asked_fact: After ordinary counteroffer, optionally exhaust Chief; proposer avoids return by paying Chief owner two capital.

whole_entry_support.quote: After a counteroffer is proposed, you may exhaust Chief Gorman to return it to its proposer’s hand unless they give you 2 capital.
The proposer can give Chief Gorman’s owner 2 capital to avoid the return.

asked_fact_assessments.asked_fact: Returned offer goes to proposer's hand; proposer ceases countering, cannot counter again that turn, and receives no refund of proposal discards.

whole_entry_support.quote: After a counteroffer is proposed, you may exhaust Chief Gorman to return it to its proposer’s hand unless they give you 2 capital.
Returning the counteroffer to its proposer’s hand ends their countering status.
They cannot propose another counteroffer this turn.
Proposal-cost discards are not refunded.

grades.rationale: Ordinary-counteroffer timing, optional exhaustion, two capital to Chief owner, return to proposer hand, loss of countering status, no repeat and sunk proposal discards are correct. No unasked revival/stack ruling is required or asserted.

grades.label: Correct

asked_fact_assessments.asked_fact: When an ordinary offer is proposed, optionally exhaust Caprice.

whole_entry_support.quote: Caprice may be used when a player proposes an offer; Unorthodox Knowledge is exempt.
When a player proposes an offer, Caprice’s owner may exhaust her.

asked_fact_assessments.asked_fact: Proposer must declare exact resolution and is bound by declaration.

whole_entry_support.quote: No. Caprice requires the proposer to declare exactly how they will resolve the action and binds them to that declaration.

grades.rationale: Offer-proposal timing, optional exhaustion, exact declaration and binding resolution are all accurately supplied.
